fixed: Figure~\ref{fig:r2m4_event_csi} compares the two decision rules using saved single-run forecasts. Under the fixed rule, Persistence CSI was 0.139 at Q95, 0.076 at Q97.5, 0.166 at 0.5~mm\,h$^{-1}$ and 0.058 at 1.0~mm\,h$^{-1}$; the six learning models reached at most 0.071, 0.009, 0.113 and 0.011, respectively. All 24 learning-model differences at these four thresholds were negative, with each pointwise 95\% paired circular-block interval below zero; this is not a multiple-comparison-adjusted claim (Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m4_fixed_events}). For example, XGBoost minus Persistence was $-0.0681$ at Q95, with interval $[-0.1131,-0.0219]$, and $-0.0533$ at 0.5~mm\,h$^{-1}$, with interval $[-0.0949,-0.0118]$. At 1.0~mm\,h$^{-1}$, the corresponding difference was $-0.0472$ with interval $[-0.0791,-0.0194]$. Several zero CSI values occurred because the predicted means never reached the fixed threshold and no event forecast was issued, not because missing scores were replaced by zero.
tuned: Validation-selected cutoffs changed the operating rule rather than removing the fixed-rule failure. At Q95, five learning models had higher CSI than the separately optimized Persistence forecast; the Transformer's difference was negative and its interval included zero. At 1.0~mm\,h$^{-1}$, four learning-model intervals supported higher CSI, while those for Transformer and Probabilistic BiLSTM-Attention included zero. Learning-model FAR was approximately 0.73--0.80 at Q95 and 0.86--0.92 at 1.0~mm\,h$^{-1}$. Their AUCs were approximately 0.80--0.85 and 0.82--0.87, respectively, compared with Persistence values of 0.747 and 0.732. This ranking information does not establish an advantage in fixed-rule CSI. Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m4_tuned_events} reports the selected cutoffs, full scores and paired intervals. Confidence intervals are conditional on the selected decision thresholds and do not account for uncertainty in threshold selection.
one_mm: At the fixed mean-based rule $c_\tau=\tau=1.0$~mm\,h$^{-1}$, XGBoost detected only one of the 91 test events, whereas the other learning models in the saved-prediction diagnostic detected none. Selecting $c_\tau$ on the validation set instead increased test POD to approximately 0.26--0.62 across these models, but FAR was approximately 0.86--0.92. Their test ROC AUC values were approximately 0.82--0.87, compared with 0.73 for persistence. Thus, the forecasts retained information for ranking exceedance events, even when their means rarely reached the event-intensity threshold. Lowering the decision cutoff recovered detections at the cost of many false alarms; it did not resolve the high-threshold event-prediction problem.
